quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 12 (RI)/TD04049_CHOS MNGON PA KUN LAS BTUS PA (Abhidharma Samuccaya)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Asaṅga, Abhidharmasamuccaya (Tōh. 4049), in the section on how the qualities (ཡོན་ཏན) are accomplished
quotes.why: The canonical source of the paragraph's first quotation. Asaṅga says 'the five abhijñās' and 'the four pure dhyānas' where the yig cha reads 'the abhijñās' and 'the pure dhyānas'. Found by direct search in the Tengyur.

quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 12 (RI)/TD04049_CHOS MNGON PA KUN LAS BTUS PA (Abhidharma Samuccaya)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Asaṅga, Abhidharmasamuccaya (Tōh. 4049), the sentence immediately following
quotes.why: The canonical source of the second quotation, on the basis of the 'remaining qualities', among them the sixth abhijñā. Unlike the sentence before it, it leaves out the non-Buddhist (ཕྱི་རོལ་པ). Found by direct search.

quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 12 (RI)/TD04049_CHOS MNGON PA KUN LAS BTUS PA (Abhidharma Samuccaya)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Asaṅga, Abhidharmasamuccaya (Tōh. 4049), definitions of the six abhijñās
quotes.why: The source behind the paragraph's 'all six rely on dhyāna'. Asaṅga opens each abhijñā definition with བསམ་གཏན་ལ་བརྟེན་ནས, so the paragraph's third quotation abbreviates these definitions rather than repeating any single sentence. Found by direct search.

quotes.citation: མངོན་རྟོགས་རྒྱན། ch. 1, the verse listing the ten instructions (གདམས་ངག)
quotes.why: The root-verse line whose sixth instruction, on the six abhijñās, is the section this paragraph belongs to. Found by direct search.

quotes.citation: འགྲེལ་པ་དོན་གསལ། ch. 1, gloss on the instruction on the six abhijñās
quotes.why: Haribhadra lists the six only by what they do (shaking the earth, hearing faint and loud sounds, and so on). He says nothing about their basis, their levels or their subdivisions, which is everything this paragraph is about. The paragraph's definitions take their wording from this passage. Found by direct search.

quotes.text: དང་པོ་ལ་ལྔ། རྟེན་གྱི་ས། བརྟེན་པའི་མཚན་ཉིད། ཁྱད་པར། ས་མཚམས། དགོས་པའོ། །
quotes.citation: ལེགས་བཤད་གསེར་ཕྲེང་སྟོད་ཆ། instruction on the six abhijñās, the object of instruction
quotes.why: Tsongkhapa's five-part scheme for the six abhijñās, the obvious model for Chökyi Gyaltsen's six-part scheme, which adds རྒྱུ.

quotes.citation: ལེགས་བཤད་གསེར་ཕྲེང་སྟོད་ཆ། same place, on the basis (རྟེན་གྱི་ས)
quotes.why: Tsongkhapa explains what 'extreme' (རབ་མཐའ) dhyāna means in Asaṅga's system and makes the same argument from the Abhidharmasamuccaya that the paragraph makes against a formless basis. This is Chökyi Gyaltsen's third proof, almost word for word.
Tsongkhapa names the Kośa's conflicting position, that the sixth abhijñā is found on every level, and sets it aside as Vaibhāṣika. Chökyi Gyaltsen's paragraph does not mention this conflict.

quotes.file: Tengyur/07 MNGON PA_Higher Knowledge School (Abhidharma)/VOL 2 (KU)/TD04089_CHOS MNGON PA'I MDZOD KYI TSIG LE'UR BYAS PA (Abhidarmakoṣa Kārikā)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Vasubandhu, Abhidharmakośakārikā (Tōh. 4089), ch. 7 on the abhijñās
quotes.why: The Kośa verse that Tsongkhapa sets aside. It agrees that the first five rest on the four dhyānas, but it treats the sixth like the power of knowing the exhaustion of contaminants. Found by direct search in the Tengyur.

quotes.file: Tengyur/07 MNGON PA_Higher Knowledge School (Abhidharma)/VOL 2 (KU)/TD04089_CHOS MNGON PA'I MDZOD KYI TSIG LE'UR BYAS PA (Abhidarmakoṣa Kārikā)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: The canonical source for dividing magical power by origin. Counting the meditation-born and birth-born kinds from the line before, it has five kinds where the paragraph has four. It also defines the divine eye and ear as clear form of the dhyāna level. Found by direct search.

quotes.citation: མཛོད་ཀྱི་སྤྱི་དོན། end of the seventh chapter (ཡེ་ཤེས)
quotes.why: Chökyi Gyaltsen's own Kośa commentary gives five kinds of magical power, including birth-attained. In this paragraph he gives four and files cakravartins and flesh-eaters under karma. Found by direct search.

quotes.citation: སྐབས་དང་པོའི་མཐའ་དཔྱོད། six abhijñās, refutation of others (a ཁ་ཅིག)
quotes.why: In his own mtha' dpyod Chökyi Gyaltsen attributes this definition to an opponent and refutes it. It is the 'with concomitant samādhi and prajñā' definition that this paragraph's wording leaves out and p419 rejects.

Chökyi Gyaltsen uses the thesis of this paragraph's first point, that the dhyāna mind is the dominant condition, to argue that the divine eye and ear abhijñās are mental and not sensory consciousness.

quotes.citation: སྐབས་དང་པོའི་མཐའ་དཔྱོད། same section, own system on the boundaries (ས་མཚམས)
quotes.why: Chökyi Gyaltsen's boundary for the sixth abhijñā: every Hīnayāna arhat who has an actual dhyāna. So 'extreme dhyāna' here cannot mean the fourth dhyāna only.

quotes.citation: རྣམ་བཤད་སྙིང་པོའི་རྒྱན། ch. 1, instruction on the six abhijñās
quotes.why: Gyaltsab Je's gloss on the magical-power abhijñā, 'concomitant with samādhi and prajñā'. It is the wording Chökyi Gyaltsen's definition avoids.

quotes.citation: རྣམ་བཤད་སྙིང་པོའི་རྒྱན། same place, on the divine eye
quotes.why: Gyaltsab Je distinguishes the divine eye, a subtle meditative form, from the abhijñā, a mental consciousness that relies on it as dominant condition. That is the model for the paragraph's 'arisen from the divine ear that is its dominant condition'.

quotes.citation: སྐབས་བརྒྱད་ཀྱི་སྤྱི་དོན་མེ་ལོང་། six abhijñās, on the mental basis
quotes.why: Jamyang Shantipa says why the 'pure' (དག་པ་བ) of Asaṅga's sentence cannot be taken strictly: a Buddha has no pure-class absorptions. This helps explain why the paragraph's thesis says 'actual dhyāna as appropriate' rather than 'pure dhyāna'.
Ngok Lotsāwa reads Asaṅga's 'extreme fourth dhyāna' as possibly requiring all nine successive absorptions and leaves the boundary open. That is a stricter reading than the Gelug one.
